reason: James in his own voice defines conversion as the case where the focus of excitement and heat comes to lie permanently within a certain (religious) system; relation, direction, and voice all match.
Identity overreach: the text says mystical states are 'more like states of feeling than like states of intellect' — an explicit comparison/analogy, not an assertion of identity.

Content and direction are correct (the divided self becomes unified), but James commits to this definition in his own voice ('This at least is what conversion signifies in general terms'), so james-asserts fits better than james-reports.

James asserts in his own voice that alcohol's sway is due to its power to stimulate the mystical faculties, and adds that drunken consciousness is one bit of the mystic consciousness; direction and voice correct.
Identity overreach: James says personal religious experience 'has its root and centre in' mystical states — a grounding relation, not identity between the two concepts.

The quoted Starbuck material (footnote 113) states conversion is 'a process of struggling away from sin rather than of striving towards righteousness'; direction and james-quotes-source typing are correct.

Wrong object, effectively reversed: Al-Ghazzali says mystical knowledge cannot be grasped by STUDY, and is grasped precisely through transport, ecstasy, and transformation — i.e. feeling-like states are the means, not the excluded route.
Conflation: the text says conversion means religious ideas move from peripheral to central in consciousness — conversion is the process of recentering, not identical with religious ideas themselves.
Directly quoted from Starbuck ('he must fall back on the larger Power that makes for righteousness'); relation, direction, and james-quotes-source typing are correct.
James's own third mark of mystical states is Transiency ('Mystical states cannot be sustained for long'); relation and voice correct.
James asserts in his own voice, before introducing the Starbuck quote, that at the last step 'self-surrender becomes then indispensable' to the unification sought in conversion.
The paragraph is a verbatim Bucke quotation stating 'The prime characteristic of cosmic consciousness is a consciousness of the cosmos'; relation and quoted-source typing correct.

Relation not asserted: James says no account of the universe can be FINAL if it disregards these other forms of consciousness — a constraint on accounts, not an identity between an account and potential forms of consciousness.
Reversed: in Teresa's testimony the orison of union yields the unshakable certitude ('a certitude which abides with her'), not the certitude yielding the union.

Wrong object: the paragraph says nitrous oxide stimulates 'the mystical consciousness'; 'firmer hold upon religious realities' is imported from the Lecture IX conversion definition and does not appear here.
Saint John of the Cross is quoted saying mystical knowledge is received 'clothed in none of the... sensible representations'; relation, direction, and quoted-source typing correct.
James asserts under the Noetic-quality mark that mystical states 'carry with them a curious sense of authority for after-time'; relation and voice correct.
Subject and object scrambled: the text reports that the Vedantists test superconsciousness's purity by its empirical fruits, not that empirical fruits test superconsciousness by Vedanta.

Wrong object: the reported doctrine is that yoga leads the disciple into samadhi and to facts 'no instinct or reason can ever know' — nothing links yoga to sensible representations, which the mystics elsewhere say are absent.
Reversed: the Starbuck quote says CONVERSION is a process of struggling away from sin, not that sin is a process of struggling away from conversion.
